abstract: Quantitative variation in inflorescence branching drives grass diversification, yet the cis-regulatory mechanisms tuning reproductive meristem activity remain poorly understood. Here, we identified a module of two CArG boxes within a conserved noncoding sequence near rice APO1. Genome-edited alleles generated a quantitative phenotypic series: deletions affecting both CArG boxes produced the strongest increases in secondary branching, whereas deletions restricted to CArG box 1 produced smaller but reproducible increases. These deletions extended secondary branch formation toward the panicle base at the expense of direct spikelets, while spikelet number per primary branch was maintained or increased. Across eight genotypes, APO1 transcript abundance was quantitatively associated with branching, and both CArG boxes contributed to MADS15-MADS34 binding to CNS3, consistent with this module limiting APO1 expression. Structural and CArG-box changes in this region were detected across multiple phylogenetically distinct lineages with branched inflorescences, indicating that APO1 underwent recurrent cis-regulatory modification during grass inflorescence diversification.
